extracted.intended_audience: foreign educational institutions seeking VA program approval; VA program administrators and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and required content for submitting VA Form 22-0976 (Application for Approval of a Program in a Foreign Country) so the Department of Veterans Affairs can determine whether a foreign program is approvable under 38 CFR 21.4260. Includes statutory compliance obligations for foreign institutions (enrollment, school liability, advertising limits) and procedural Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission/comment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability under 38 CFR 21.4260
rubrics_metrics.description: VA will use the information collected to determine if a program in a foreign country is approvable under CFR 21.4260.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order for a review and decision to be made, the VA needs supporting information from a foreign educational institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of VA Form 22-0976 (Application for Approval of a Program in a Foreign Country)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Application for Approval of a Program in a Foreign Country, VA Form 22-0976 OMB ICR #2900-0853 is being submitted as a 'Revision'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revision changes formatting and most existing questions to statements; the revised form is the official application that all foreign institutions must use to formally request foreign program approval for GI Bill benefits from VA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form content should be statements (not YES/NO questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently, the VA Form 22-0976 questions are written to solicit YES/NO responses regarding compliance to the current and new provisions established for foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form questions should instead be written and displayed in the form of a statement to indicate the VA requirements necessary for the achievement of compliance for foreign institutions. (The agency states there is no change to current burden as a result of making these revisions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to allow continued enrollment pending VA payment (Section 104 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign institutions must allow eligible individuals to stay enrolled in courses of education pending the receipt of educational assistance from Department of Veterans Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution's policy must ensure that they will not impose any penalty, including the assessment of late fees, the denial of access to classes, libraries, or other institutional facilities, or make it a requirement that a covered individual borrow additional funds because of the individual's inability to meet his or her financial obligations to the institution due to the delayed disbursement funding from VA under chapter 31 or 33.

rubrics_metrics.name: School liability for payments (Section 1019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1019 requires schools and training programs to be financially responsible (School Liability), instead of the student, for payments which are directly paid to an educational institution pursuant to the Post-9/11 GI Bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include payments paid to an educational institution pursuant to the Yellow Ribbon GI Education Enhancement program and the advance payments of the initial educational assistance to an institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on advertising, sales, and marketing; prohibition on deceptive practices (Section 1020)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1020 limits the type of Advertising, Sales, and Marketing that schools can conduct and remain eligible for GI Bill funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section would create a tiered penalty system against institutions that do not comply with the law and set up a mechanism for institutions to work with the SAAs and VA on coming back into compliance, and for institutions to not engage in advertising and/or enrollment practices of any type, which are erroneous, deceptive, or misleading either by actual statement, omission, or intimidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRA submission must describe the nature of the information collection and its expected cost and burden and include the actual data collection instrument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number. Written comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection revision should be sent within 30 days of publication of this notice to www.reginfo.gov/public/do/PRAMain and refer to 'OMB Control No. 2900-0853.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information about estimated burden and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: The information collection must include estimated burden metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice provides: Affected Public: Education Institutions; Estimated Annual Burden: 338 hours; Estimated Average Burden Time per Respondent: 20 minutes; Frequency of Response: Once; Estimated Number of Respondents: 1014.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision purpose: comply with statutory changes (Public Law 116-135 and Public Law 115-407)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of revising VA Form 22-0976 is to support the provisions of Public Law 116-135 and the Veterans Benefits and Transition Act of 2018, Public Law 115-407 necessary in order for foreign institutions to acknowledge and adhere to statutory requirements (including Section 104).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current form is inadequate to comply with both the current and new changes in the law; revisions will ensure the form supports new statutory provisions (e.g., enrollment protections, school liability, advertising limits).
